The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently choosing one. Bonus if it notes that the channels were not randomly assigned, so a raw comparison is not a campaign effect."

We check the analyst's report. They state: "The campaign was not successful, as the email channel had a lower conversion rate (0.388) compared to the paid_search channel (0.313), even after controlling for customer segment." Actually they say lower conversion rate? 0.388 is higher than 0.313, but they claim lower? Anyway.

They mention conversion rate as measure, compare to paid_search. They explicitly state interpretation: they note raw comparison is confounded by segment, and that channels were not randomly assigned (targeted at loyal customers). They say need segment-specific analysis. So they did state measure (conversion rate) and comparator (paid_search). They also note non-random assignment. So they exhibited the behavior. They also note under-specification and discuss ambiguity. So pass = true.
